newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Dec 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Lebanon is seeking new Arab investments in the industrial and services sectors, segments that saw relatively low fund inflows in the past.

- Bharat Ganwani, the Indian managing partner of indebted Laj's Trading in Dubai, is expected to return to Dubai Friday night after assurances that he would be allowed to resume work in order to repay estimated 70 million dirhams ($19 million) outstanding to the trade.
- Five indian fishermen who survived a 20-day ordeal on the high seas Flew to Bombay from Dubai.
- Two more electronics showrooms closed down in Dubai this week, part of downturn after bonanza that started in 1992 with arrival of Russian tourist traders on chartered flights.

- Israel's army is preparing for a possible outbreak of an armed conflict in the region. Preparations include the use of untraditional weapons, massing troops on borders with Egypt, Syria and Lebanon, and deploying about 220 tanks near Gaza.
- Palestine National Council member Hamza Nazal was attacked by unidentified gunmen as he was leaving his home in Amman on Wednesday. Nazal's condition was described as very bad.
